A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bodipy-quinone dyad can be considered as a molecular switch that is sensitive to both solvent polarity and oxidation state.
Bodipy-quinone dyads show fluorescence, exciplex formation, charge transfer and triplet formation depending on the substitution pattern.
the Bodipy unit can act as an efficient energy donor in the formation of an exciplex with the hydroquinone unit, but the Bodipy unit is a poor energy donor in the charge-separated state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Bodipy derivatives can be used as a model system for the investigation of excited state deactivation processes.
the Bodipy unit can be used as an efficient donor in the formation of charge-separated states, and that the Bodipy triplet states can be accessed from the exciplexes.
the Bodipy unit is a good donor for quinones in the ground state, but not necessarily in the excited state.
